title: Refreshing overrides does not refresh already-created singleton handlers
reasoning: refresh_overrides claims to refresh runtime overrides on an existing ApiContainer, but the target container builds handlers and the registry as Singleton providers. If get_handler_registry has already materialized handler_registry or any handler, changing dependency overrides afterward only changes provider wiring for future creations; it does not replace cached singleton handler instances that already captured the old session_manager, model_service, config, or other dependencies. A facade that expects refresh_overrides to rebind runtime dependencies can continue dispatching through stale handlers.
recommendation: When refreshing overrides after creation, either reset the affected singleton providers before the next registry lookup, rebuild the ApiContainer, or make refresh_overrides explicitly no-op unless nothing has been materialized. Keep the behavior documented in the binder contract.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No linked tests were included for this feature, and the shown code has no regression coverage asserting that handler dependencies change after refresh_overrides is called post-materialization.
suggestedRegressionTest: Create an ApiRuntimeBinder with a fake parent container, materialize the registry, replace the parent session_manager/model_service, call refresh_overrides, then assert dispatched handlers use the replacement dependency rather than the original one.
minimumFixScope: ApiRuntimeBinder refresh lifecycle plus focused container lifecycle tests.
